questions.question: What specific international resolutions and national lists must a commercial bank consider to comply with government orders related to the UAPA and WMD Act?
questions.answer: A commercial bank must consider other United Nations Security Council Resolutions (UNSCRs) and the lists detailed in the first and fourth schedules of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967, along with any subsequent amendments to these lists.
questions.evidence: the bank shall take into account: (1) other UNSCRs and (2) lists in the first schedule and the fourth schedule of UAPA, 1967 and any amendments to the same

questions.question: For what specific purpose must a commercial bank take into account UNSCRs and the UAPA lists?
questions.answer: A commercial bank must take these into account to ensure compliance with Government orders concerning the implementation of section 51A of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act and section 12A of the Weapons of Mass Destruction Act.
questions.evidence: for compliance with the Government orders on implementation of section 51A of the UAPA and section 12A of the WMD Act.

unanswerable.question: What is the required frequency for a commercial bank to review the lists in the first and fourth schedules of the UAPA, 1967, for compliance purposes?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph specifies *what* lists a commercial bank must consider but does not provide any information regarding the frequency or schedule for reviewing these lists.

questions.question: What are the primary responsibilities of a commercial bank regarding the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2010?
questions.answer: A commercial bank must ensure it adheres to the provisions of the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2010, and any rules made under it.
questions.evidence: The bank shall ensure adherence to the provisions of Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2010, and Rules made thereunder.

questions.question: Beyond the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2010 itself, what other directives must a commercial bank follow concerning foreign contributions?
questions.answer: Commercial banks must also meticulously comply with any instructions or communications issued periodically by the Reserve Bank of India, especially those based on advice from the Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India.
questions.evidence: Further, the bank shall also ensure meticulous compliance with any instructions / communications on the matter issued from time to time by the RBI based on advice received from the Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India.

unanswerable.question: What is the specific deadline for a commercial bank to submit its annual compliance report regarding the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2010, to the Reserve Bank of India?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph mandates adherence to the Act and compliance with RBI instructions but does not specify any reporting deadlines or the frequency of such reports. It only states that instructions will be issued 'from time to time'.

questions.question: What is the minimum frequency for a Commercial Bank to review its Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Risk Assessment?
questions.answer: A Commercial Bank must review its Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Risk Assessment at least annually.
questions.evidence: However, the bank shall review it at least annually.

questions.question: What factors should a Commercial Bank consider when conducting its Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Risk Assessment?
questions.answer: When conducting its Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Risk Assessment, a Commercial Bank should consider all relevant risk factors for clients, countries, products, services, transactions, or delivery channels, and also take into account any sector-specific vulnerabilities shared by the regulator or supervisor.
questions.evidence: The assessment process shall consider all the relevant risk factors before determining the level of overall risk... While preparing the internal risk assessment, the bank shall take cognizance of the overall sector-specific vulnerabilities, if any, that the regulator / supervisor may share with the bank from time to time.

unanswerable.question: Within what timeframe must a Commercial Bank present the outcome of its Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Risk Assessment to its Board or a delegated committee?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph states that the outcome must be presented to the Board or a committee, but it does not specify any deadline or timeframe for this presentation.

questions.question: For a Commercial Bank, what actions are required before temporarily suspending an existing customer's account due to their failure to submit a PAN or equivalent document?
questions.answer: A Commercial Bank must first provide the customer with an accessible notice and a reasonable opportunity to be heard before temporarily suspending operations in their account.
questions.evidence: Provided that before temporarily ceasing operations for an account, the bank shall give the customer an accessible notice and a reasonable opportunity to be heard.

questions.question: What specific provisions must a Commercial Bank include in its internal policy regarding existing customers who are unable to provide their PAN or equivalent documents due to certain personal circumstances?
questions.answer: A Commercial Bank's internal policy must include appropriate relaxations for continued operation of accounts for customers who cannot provide PAN due to injury, illness, infirmity on account of old age, or similar causes. However, these accounts will be subject to enhanced monitoring.
questions.evidence: Further, the bank shall include, in its internal policy, appropriate relaxation(s) for continued operation of accounts for customers who are unable to provide PAN or equivalent e-document thereof or Form No. 60 owing to injury, illness or infirmity on account of old age or otherwise, and such like causes.

unanswerable.question: What is the specific deadline by which Commercial Banks must obtain the PAN or equivalent e-document from their existing customers?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph states that the Central Government will notify this date, but the paragraph itself does not provide the specific date.

questions.question: What are Commercial Banks required to do regarding the 'at par' cheque facility they offer to co-operative banks?
questions.answer: A Commercial Bank must monitor and review the 'at par' cheque facility arrangements it has with co-operative banks to assess potential risks like credit and reputational risks.
questions.evidence: The ‘at par’ cheque facility offered by the bank to co-operative banks shall be monitored and such arrangements be reviewed to assess the risks including credit risk and reputational risk arising therefrom.

questions.question: What right does a Commercial Bank have concerning the records of co-operative banks that use its 'at par' cheque facility?
questions.answer: A Commercial Bank retains the right to inspect the records maintained by its customer co-operative banks or societies to ensure they comply with current KYC and AML instructions under these 'at par' cheque arrangements.
questions.evidence: The right to verify the records maintained by the customer cooperative banks / societies for compliance with the extant instructions on KYC and AML under such arrangements shall be retained by bank.

unanswerable.question: How frequently must a Commercial Bank review its 'at par' cheque facility arrangements with co-operative banks?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph states that these arrangements 'shall be monitored and such arrangements be reviewed,' but it does not specify any frequency, deadline, or periodicity for these reviews.

questions.question: For a Commercial Bank, what are the permissible payment methods for remittances of funds or the issuance of travellers' cheques valued at ₹50,000 or more?
questions.answer: For remittances or travellers' cheques valued at ₹50,000 and above, a Commercial Bank must effect the payment by debiting the customer's account or against cheques. Cash payments are not permitted for these transactions.
questions.evidence: Any remittance of funds by way of demand draft, mail / telegraphic transfer / NEFT / IMPS or any other mode and issue of travellers’ cheques for value of ₹50,000 and above shall be effected by debit to the customer’s account or against cheques and not against cash payment.

questions.question: What is the requirement for a Commercial Bank regarding the purchaser's name on instruments like demand drafts, and when did this requirement become effective?
questions.answer: A Commercial Bank is required to incorporate the name of the purchaser on the face of instruments such as demand drafts, pay orders, and banker's cheques. This instruction took effect for such instruments issued on or after September 15, 2018.
questions.evidence: Further, the bank shall incorporate the name of the purchaser on the face of the demand draft, pay order, banker’s cheque, etc., by the issuing bank. These instructions shall take effect for such instruments issued on or after September 15, 2018.

unanswerable.question: For a Commercial Bank, what specific details of the purchaser's identity (e.g., full name, initials, address, or ID number) must be incorporated on the face of a demand draft?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph states that 'the name of the purchaser' must be incorporated but does not specify what level of detail or additional identifying information is required for the purchaser's identity on the instrument.

questions.question: What specific actions must a commercial bank take regarding business relationships and transactions with individuals or entities from countries that the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) has identified as not sufficiently applying its recommendations?
questions.answer: A commercial bank must apply enhanced due diligence measures that are effective and proportionate to the risks involved, and give special attention to these business relationships and transactions.
questions.evidence: The bank shall apply enhanced due diligence measures, which are effective and proportionate to the risks, to business relationships and transactions... The bank shall give special attention to business relationships and transactions with persons... from or in countries that do not or insufficiently apply the FATF Recommendations.

questions.question: What are the documentation and retention requirements for a commercial bank when examining transactions with individuals or entities from jurisdictions listed in FATF Statements or those not adequately implementing FATF Recommendations?
questions.answer: A commercial bank must examine the background and purpose of such transactions, keep written findings along with all supporting documents, and make them available to the Reserve Bank of India or other relevant authorities upon request.
questions.evidence: The bank shall examine the background and purpose of transactions with persons... retain written findings together with all documents, and make them available to the RBI / other relevant authorities, on request.

unanswerable.question: What is the minimum duration for a commercial bank to retain the written findings and documents related to transactions with persons from jurisdictions included in FATF Statements?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph states that the bank must 'retain written findings together with all documents' but does not specify a minimum retention period (e.g., 5 years, 10 years).

questions.question: What is the general obligation for a commercial bank regarding the collection of account payee cheques for individuals or entities that are not the named payee?
questions.answer: A commercial bank is generally prohibited from collecting account payee cheques for any person or entity other than the constituent who is the named payee on the cheque.
questions.evidence: The bank shall not collect account payee cheques for any person other than the payee constituent.

questions.question: Under what specific conditions may a commercial bank choose to collect an account payee cheque for a customer that is a co-operative credit society?
questions.answer: A commercial bank has the option to collect account payee cheques for its co-operative credit society customers, provided the cheque amount does not exceed ₹50,000 and the original payees of those cheques are also constituents of that co-operative credit society.
questions.evidence: The bank shall, at its option, collect account payee cheques drawn for an amount not exceeding ₹50,000 to the account of its customers who are co-operative credit societies, provided the payees of such cheques are the constituents of such co-operative credit societies.

unanswerable.question: Can a commercial bank, at its discretion, collect an account payee cheque for a customer that is a self-help group (SHG), provided the cheque amount is below a certain threshold and the original payee is a member of that SHG?
unanswerable.why: The provided paragraph only specifies an exception for co-operative credit societies regarding the collection of account payee cheques under certain conditions. It does not mention any provisions or conditions for other types of customer entities like self-help groups.

questions.question: What is a commercial bank's obligation regarding implementing countermeasures when requested by international bodies?
questions.answer: A commercial bank must undertake countermeasures if called upon by an international or intergovernmental organization that India is a member of and that the Central Government has accepted.
questions.evidence: The bank shall undertake countermeasures when called upon so to do by any international or intergovernmental organisation of which India is a member and which is accepted by the Central Government.

questions.question: Which specific types of international organizations can require a commercial bank to implement countermeasures?
questions.answer: A commercial bank is required to implement countermeasures when requested by an international or intergovernmental organization that India is a member of and that has been accepted by the Central Government.
questions.evidence: The bank shall undertake countermeasures when called upon so to do by any international or intergovernmental organisation of which India is a member and which is accepted by the Central Government.

unanswerable.question: What is the maximum timeframe a commercial bank has to implement countermeasures once requested by an accepted international organization?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph specifies the conditions under which a commercial bank must undertake countermeasures but does not provide any deadlines or timeframes for their implementation.

questions.question: As a compliance officer at a Commercial Bank, I need to understand how the RBI (Commercial Banks – Know Your Customer) Directions, 2025 interact with other existing laws or regulations concerning KYC. Do these Directions replace or diminish the requirements of other applicable laws?
questions.answer: No, the RBI (Commercial Banks – Know Your Customer) Directions, 2025 do not replace or diminish the requirements of other laws. Instead, their provisions are intended to be supplementary to any other laws, rules, regulations, or directions currently in force.
questions.evidence: The provisions of these Directions shall be in addition to, and not in derogation of the provisions of any other laws, rules, regulations, or directions, for the time being in force.

unanswerable.question: If a specific provision within the RBI (Commercial Banks – Know Your Customer) Directions, 2025 directly conflicts with a provision in another existing law or regulation, which provision takes precedence for a Commercial Bank?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph states that the Directions are 'in addition to, and not in derogation of' other laws, implying they supplement rather than override. However, it does not provide a specific mechanism or rule for resolving a direct contradiction or conflict between a provision in these Directions and a provision in another law, only that these Directions do not lessen the effect of other laws.

questions.question: For what purposes can a commercial bank utilize the Video-based Customer Identification Process (V-CIP)?
questions.answer: A commercial bank can use V-CIP for Customer Due Diligence (CDD) when onboarding new individual customers, proprietors of proprietorship firms, or authorized signatories and Beneficial Owners of Legal Entity customers. It can also be used for converting existing accounts opened with Aadhaar OTP based e-KYC, and for updating or periodically updating KYC for eligible customers.
questions.evidence: The bank may undertake V-CIP to carry out: (1) CDD in case of new customer onboarding for individual customers, proprietor in case of proprietorship firm, authorised signatories and Beneficial Owners (BOs) in case of Legal Entity (LE) customers. (2) Conversion of existing accounts opened in non-face-to-face mode using Aadhaar OTP based e-KYC authentication as per paragraph 25. (3) Updation / Periodic updation of KYC for eligible customers.

questions.question: When a commercial bank uses V-CIP for a proprietorship firm, what additional documentation is required beyond the proprietor's Customer Due Diligence?
questions.answer: When a commercial bank undertakes V-CIP for a proprietorship firm, it must also obtain the equivalent e-documents of the activity proofs pertaining to the proprietorship firm, in addition to completing the Customer Due Diligence for the proprietor.
questions.evidence: Provided that in case of CDD of a proprietorship firm, the bank shall also obtain the equivalent e-document of the activity proofs with respect to the proprietorship firm, as mentioned in paragraph 31 and paragraph 32, apart from undertaking CDD of the proprietor.

unanswerable.question: What specific activity proofs are required for a proprietorship firm when a commercial bank uses V-CIP for Customer Due Diligence?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph states that activity proofs are required and refers to paragraphs 31 and 32 for details, but it does not list the specific proofs itself.

questions.question: What is a Commercial Bank's obligation regarding ongoing due diligence for its customers?
questions.answer: A Commercial Bank is required to perform ongoing due diligence on its customers.
questions.evidence: The bank shall undertake ongoing due diligence of customers

questions.question: What aspects should a Commercial Bank consider when performing ongoing due diligence for its customers?
questions.answer: A Commercial Bank must ensure that customer transactions are consistent with the bank's knowledge of the customer, their business and risk profile, and the origin of their funds or wealth.
questions.evidence: to ensure that their transactions are consistent with their knowledge about the customers, customers’ business and risk profile, the source of funds / wealth.

unanswerable.question: What specific actions constitute 'ongoing due diligence' that a Commercial Bank must perform?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph states that ongoing due diligence must be undertaken and specifies its purpose, but it does not detail the specific actions or procedures involved in performing this due diligence.

questions.question: How many documents proving business activity must a commercial bank collect from a sole proprietary firm for customer due diligence?
questions.answer: A commercial bank must obtain any two documents as proof of business or activity for a sole proprietary firm.
questions.evidence: the bank shall also obtain any two of the following documents or the equivalent e-documents thereof as proof of business / activity in the name of the proprietary firm

questions.question: Can a commercial bank accept a Udyam Registration Certificate and utility bills as proof of business activity for a sole proprietary firm?
questions.answer: Yes, a commercial bank can accept a Udyam Registration Certificate and utility bills (such as electricity, water, or landline telephone bills) as proof of business activity for a sole proprietary firm.
questions.evidence: (1) Registration certificate including Udyam Registration Certificate (URC) issued by the Government. ... (8) Utility bills such as electricity, water, landline telephone bills, etc.

unanswerable.question: What is the maximum age allowed for the utility bills submitted by a sole proprietary firm as proof of business activity?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph lists utility bills as an acceptable document but does not specify any validity period or maximum age for these documents.

questions.question: When a Commercial Bank opens a savings bank account for a Self Help Group (SHG), what are the requirements for Customer Due Diligence (CDD) concerning the SHG members?
questions.answer: A Commercial Bank is not required to perform Customer Due Diligence (CDD) on all members of a Self Help Group (SHG) when opening its savings bank account. Instead, CDD on only the office bearers of the SHG is sufficient.
questions.evidence: (1) The bank shall not require CDD of all the members of an SHG while opening the savings bank account of the SHG. (2) The CDD of all the office bearers shall suffice.

questions.question: Is a Commercial Bank permitted to conduct Customer Due Diligence (CDD) on all members of a Self Help Group (SHG) at any point?
questions.answer: Yes, a Commercial Bank has the discretion to undertake Customer Due Diligence (CDD) of all members of a Self Help Group (SHG) specifically at the time of credit linking the SHG.
questions.evidence: (3) The bank may undertake CDD of all the members of an SHG at the time of credit linking of SHGs.

unanswerable.question: What specific documents are required for the Customer Due Diligence (CDD) of the office bearers of a Self Help Group (SHG) when a Commercial Bank opens its savings account?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph states that CDD of office bearers shall suffice but does not specify the particular documents or procedures required for this CDD.
